plan.topic: How long tirzepatide takes to work: a timeline of appetite, blood sugar, weight and blood pressure based on the published randomized trials (SURMOUNT-1 in adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks; SURPASS trials in type 2 diabetes)
plan.angle: How long tirzepatide takes to work, measure by measure. Weight (SURMOUNT-1: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, 72 weeks): use only the numbers the NEJM paper reports, or figures read approximately from its graph and labelled 'about'. Give per-arm group sizes and the estimand. Blood sugar (SURPASS, type 2 diabetes only): HbA1c at the reported timepoints. Blood pressure: only at the timepoints the trials reported (SURMOUNT-1, week 72). Appetite: explained as mechanism, with no week-by-week claims unless a named human study measured it. Say the trials raised the dose gradually by design, with no numbers. 'Averages, not predictions.' Plateau and slower responders. Common GI side effects are most frequent early on, plus habits with their caveats. Don't change, stop or switch on your own. CTA: an already-published Lane A or Life on GLP-1 long-form, not 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?'. Prescriber line.

plan.why: A Lane A search-question title the playbook names itself. People search it constantly, it rests on peer-reviewed RCT data, and it doesn't repeat any Short from the last 14 days. | fact-check: Good Lane A search topic with an evergreen question and solid trial data (SURMOUNT-1 in NEJM 2022, the SURPASS program). Three changes are needed. (1) Appetite chapter: SURMOUNT-1 did not measure a timeline of appetite or 'food noise'. Don't give an appetite timeline unless the script cites a specific published human study that measured appetite or energy intake at named weeks. If no such study is cited, present appetite as how the drug works, with no week claims. (2) Blood pressure: only use timepoints the trials actually reported (SURMOUNT-1's main BP result is change at week 72). Don't make up an early-weeks BP timeline. (3) Weight at month 3, 6 and 12: read off the published figure, these are approximations. Say 'about' and 'read from the trial's published graph', or use only time points the paper reports in numbers. Keep the per-arm group sizes, the estimand and 'averages, not predictions'. Explain plainly that early results partly reflect the trial's built-in gradual dose increase, with no numbers or schedules. CTA problem: the playbook flags 'Did Retatrutide Beat Tirzepatide?' as a banned frame with no head-to-head trial behind it, and it's in a different lane. Sending Lane A viewers there undermines the experiment and points them to an indirect comparison. Name an already-published Lane A or 'Life on GLP-1' long-form instead. If none exists, use the end screen plus 'follow the Life on GLP-1 series'. Keep the GI side-effects line, the fluids caveat ('unless you've been told to limit fluids'), the protein caveat (check first if you have kidney disease), 'don't change, stop or switch on your own' and the prescriber line. Title: 'How Long Does Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Take to Work?' is 51 characters with no numbers or abbreviations, so it's OK.

package.description:
How long tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) takes to work depends on what you're measuring. In SURPASS-1 (adults with type 2 diabetes, not on diabetes medicines), A1C was measured at week 40. In SURMOUNT-1 (adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes), average weight fell for most of 72 weeks. Side effects were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal ones, like nausea and diarrhea, mainly while the dose was being raised. Trial averages, not predictions.

Tirzepatide is a prescription medicine. This video is education, not personal medical advice. Don't change, stop or switch any medicine on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

Sources:
1. Jastreboff AM et al. "Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity." New England Journal of Medicine, 2022. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2206038
2. Rosenstock J et al. "Efficacy and safety of a novel dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide in patients with type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-1): a double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial." The Lancet, 2021. https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(21)01324-6/fulltext

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: The main weight trial is SURMOUNT-1, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in twenty twenty-two. It enrolled adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes.

visual.stock_query: medical journal on desk with spotlight

scenes.retention_device: Micro-story setup of the key trial

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: Two thousand five hundred thirty-nine people were randomly assigned for seventy-two weeks: six hundred forty-three to placebo, six hundred thirty to five milligrams, six hundred thirty-six to ten milligrams, and six hundred thirty to fifteen milligrams.

visual.stock_query: four groups of cartoon people

scenes.retention_device: Concrete numbers with per-arm group sizes

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: Everyone, placebo group included, also got lifestyle counseling on diet and activity.

visual.stock_query: coach chatting with group about meals and walking

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: Now here's the part most people miss. Nobody started on their final dose. By design, the trial raised the dose gradually, step by step, over the first several months.

visual.stock_query: gentle staircase climbing upward, hopeful

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: So the early weeks don't show the full-dose effect. A slow first month was partly how the trial was built.

visual.myth: A slow first month means it isn't working
visual.fact: In SURMOUNT-1, early weeks came before people reached their assigned dose
visual.stock_query: turtle starting a long race, smiling

scenes.retention_device: Pays off the first-month loop; relief beat

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: The headline weight numbers count everyone randomized, whether or not they kept taking the medicine. That's the treatment-regimen estimand, the more cautious way to count.
scenes.on_screen_text: Everyone counted, even if they stopped

visual.stock_query: scientist counting every person in a crowd

scenes.section: How were the trials set up?
scenes.narration: And every number you'll hear is a group average. Averages, not predictions. Your body writes its own timeline.

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: Let's start with appetite, and that constant background chatter some call food noise.

visual.stock_query: brain with chattering food thought bubbles

scenes.retention_device: Chapter card on the most-discussed effect

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: Tirzepatide activates receptors for two natural gut hormones, GLP-1 and GIP. Your body already releases these hormones around meals.

visual.stock_query: two friendly hormone characters leaving the gut

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: GLP-1 signals reach brain areas involved in hunger and fullness, which is thought to be a big part of how these medicines help people eat less.

visual.stock_query: calm brain receiving a gentle message

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: Tirzepatide also slows how quickly your stomach empties, so a meal stays with you longer.

visual.stock_query: relaxed stomach character holding a meal

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: But here's where it gets interesting. According to the official prescribing information, that stomach-slowing effect is largest after the very first dose, and it gets smaller over time.

visual.stock_query: surprised stomach character with shrinking arrow

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: Is there a week-by-week appetite timeline? Honestly, SURMOUNT-1 didn't measure one. It tracked weight and health markers, not food noise.

visual.myth: There's a proven day-by-day appetite schedule
visual.fact: SURMOUNT-1 tracked weight and health markers, not food noise
visual.stock_query: empty calendar with question marks, honest mood

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: For Dana, that's freeing. If her hunger shifted early, great. If it didn't, that alone isn't proof anything is wrong.
scenes.on_screen_text: No early shift? Not proof of failure

visual.stock_query: woman exhaling with relief at kitchen table

scenes.section: When does tirzepatide start working on appetite?
scenes.narration: But appetite is a feeling. Blood sugar is a number, and that clock has much harder data.

visual.stock_query: glucose meter character ready to reveal

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: This part applies to adults with type 2 diabetes.

visual.stock_query: blood sugar meter with friendly face

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Tirzepatide helps the pancreas release insulin when blood sugar is high, and lowers glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar.

visual.stock_query: pancreas character releasing insulin keys

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Doctors track this with a test called A-one-C, which reflects average blood sugar over roughly three months. It's slow-moving by design.

visual.stock_query: slow snail carrying a blood test tube

scenes.retention_device: Analogy explaining why results take time

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: The cleanest test of tirzepatide alone was SURPASS-1, in The Lancet, twenty twenty-one: adults with type 2 diabetes not controlled by diet and exercise, and not on diabetes medicines.

visual.stock_query: journal cover with spotlight, curious researchers

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Four hundred seventy-eight people, for forty weeks: one hundred fifteen on placebo and one hundred twenty-one in each of the five, ten and fifteen milligram groups. Average starting A-one-C: seven point nine percent.

visual.stock_query: four small groups of people

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: By week forty, counting people while they stayed on their assigned treatment, A-one-C fell by one point eight seven, one point eight nine and two point oh seven percentage points across the three tirzepatide groups. On placebo, it rose by zero point oh four.

visual.stock_query: blood sugar meter cheering small win

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Counting people while they stayed on treatment, eighty-seven, ninety-two and eighty-eight percent in the tirzepatide groups reached an A-one-C below seven percent by week forty, a common goal. On placebo, nineteen percent did.

visual.stat_label: On treatment: tirzepatide A1C below 7%, week 40
visual.stock_query: people crossing a finish line together

scenes.retention_device: Humanised payoff: most reached the goal

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: Week forty is when the result was measured, not when the drug started acting.

visual.stock_query: stopwatch photo finish, thoughtful

scenes.retention_device: Reframe that sets up the next clock

scenes.section: How fast does tirzepatide lower blood sugar?
scenes.narration: But most people are watching the scale, and that clock runs longer.

visual.stock_query: bathroom scale with long winding road

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Back to SURMOUNT-1, and the scale.

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Reading approximately from the trial's published graph, average weight in all three tirzepatide groups started falling within the first weeks and kept falling for most of the seventy-two weeks.
scenes.on_screen_text: About: read from the trial graph

visual.stock_query: gently sloping line graph with friendly arrow

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: The curves only gradually flattened in the later months: change unfolding over many months, not one.

visual.stock_query: curve leveling off on a hillside, calm

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Here are the numbers the paper reports. At week seventy-two, counting everyone randomized, average weight loss was fifteen percent on five milligrams, nineteen point five percent on ten, and twenty point nine percent on fifteen. On placebo, three point one percent.

visual.stock_query: Medi cheering beside bar chart

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: That's roughly one fifth of body weight, but it's an average across six hundred thirty people. Some lost more, some less.

visual.stock_query: pie with one fifth highlighted, crowd behind

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Counting only people while they stayed on treatment, the averages were sixteen, twenty-one point four and twenty-two point five percent, versus two point four percent on placebo. That's the efficacy estimand.

visual.stock_query: second chart labelled on treatment

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: In the trial, week three meant still early in the gradual dose increase, at the very start of a seventy-two-week curve. That's where Dana is.
scenes.on_screen_text: Week 3 = start of a long curve

visual.stock_query: woman at start of a long path, sunrise

scenes.section: When does weight loss start on tirzepatide?

visual.stock_query: locked box with question mark, teasing

scenes.section: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure?
scenes.narration: SURMOUNT-1 reported its main blood pressure result at week seventy-two.

visual.stock_query: friendly blood pressure cuff character

scenes.section: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure?
scenes.narration: Pooled across the three tirzepatide doses, systolic blood pressure, the top number, fell by an average of seven point two millimeters of mercury, versus one point zero on placebo.

visual.stock_query: relaxed heart character with gauge

scenes.section: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure?
scenes.narration: The bottom number, diastolic pressure, fell by four point eight on tirzepatide, versus zero point eight on placebo.

visual.stock_query: gauge needle easing down

scenes.section: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure?
scenes.narration: The main paper gives no early blood pressure timeline, so we won't invent one. If you check at home, share your readings with your prescriber, especially if you take blood pressure medicines.

visual.stock_query: person showing home readings to doctor, calm

scenes.section: Does tirzepatide lower blood pressure?
scenes.narration: Which brings us to the question behind so many late-night searches: why am I not losing weight yet?

visual.stock_query: person searching on phone in bed at night

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Here's the number I promised. Losing at least five percent of body weight is a common benchmark.

visual.stock_query: unlocked box revealing a number

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: In SURMOUNT-1, counting everyone randomized, eighty-five, eighty-nine and ninety-one percent of the five, ten and fifteen milligram groups reached it by week seventy-two. On placebo, thirty-five percent did.

visual.stock_query: most people crossing a line

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Now flip it around. Counting everyone randomized, including people who stopped the medicine, roughly nine to fifteen people in every hundred in the tirzepatide groups had not reached five percent at week seventy-two.

visual.stat_label: Tirzepatide groups, all randomized, under 5%, week 72
visual.stock_query: small group of people, warm support

scenes.retention_device: The hidden number revealed (main loop paid off)

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: That's what 'averages, not predictions' means. If your response is slower or smaller than average, you're not failing, and it's not a character flaw.

visual.stock_query: Medi reassuring a worried person

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Plateaus fit too: even the average curves slowed in the later months.

visual.stock_query: hiker resting on a flat ridge

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: If progress feels slow or stalled, bring it to your prescriber, who can look at the whole picture. Please don't change, stop or switch on your own.

visual.stock_query: patient and doctor talking kindly

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: So what happens if someone stops? A separate trial tested exactly that.

visual.stock_query: fork in the road, curious

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: In SURMOUNT-4, adults with obesity or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes, took tirzepatide for thirty-six weeks. Then six hundred seventy were randomized: three hundred thirty-five continued, three hundred thirty-five switched to placebo.

visual.stock_query: group splitting into two equal paths

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: Over the next fifty-two weeks, counting everyone randomized, weight in the placebo group went back up by an average of fourteen percent, while the group that continued lost a further five point five percent.

visual.stock_query: two lines diverging on a chart

scenes.section: Why am I not losing weight on tirzepatide?
scenes.narration: So the clock doesn't simply stop at week seventy-two. That's why decisions about stopping belong with your prescriber.

visual.stock_query: clock still ticking, doctor nearby

scenes.section: Are side effects worse in the first weeks?
scenes.narration: Now the part that clustered early: side effects.

visual.stock_query: queasy stomach character with calm cloud

scenes.section: Are side effects worse in the first weeks?
scenes.narration: In SURMOUNT-1, the most common side effects were gastrointestinal, like nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting. Most were mild to moderate, and they happened mainly during the dose-increase phase.

visual.stock_query: tummy character with gentle wavy lines

scenes.section: Are side effects worse in the first weeks?
scenes.narration: Some people did stop because of side effects: four point three, seven point one and six point two percent in the five, ten and fifteen milligram groups, versus two point six percent on placebo.

visual.stock_query: small figures stepping off a path

scenes.section: Are side effects worse in the first weeks?
scenes.narration: That's the frustrating overlap: side effects clustered early, while weight had the furthest to go. Knowing the pattern can make the early weeks feel less like failure.

visual.stock_query: two timelines overlapping, person understanding

scenes.section: Are side effects worse in the first weeks?
scenes.narration: The prescribing information warns that vomiting and diarrhea can cause dehydration, which can affect the kidneys. Contact your prescriber if side effects are severe or persistent, and seek care for severe stomach pain that won't go away.

visual.stock_query: person phoning clinic, calm

scenes.section: What helps in the first months?
scenes.narration: What helps while the clocks run? Habits worth discussing with your care team.

visual.stock_query: Medi with toolbox of healthy habits

scenes.section: What helps in the first months?
scenes.narration: Try smaller meals, eaten slowly, and stop when you feel comfortably full. With food leaving the stomach more slowly, big portions can sit heavier.

visual.stock_query: small colorful plate, person eating slowly

scenes.section: What helps in the first months?
scenes.narration: Drink fluids regularly through the day, unless you've been told to limit fluids. It matters even more if nausea or diarrhea shows up.

visual.stock_query: water glass with cheerful face

scenes.section: What helps in the first months?
scenes.narration: Build meals around a protein source. If you have kidney disease, check with your doctor first about how much protein is right for you.

visual.stock_query: salmon beans and eggs on plate

scenes.section: What helps in the first months?
scenes.narration: Add some strength training, and start gently. US guidelines recommend muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week for adults.

factcheck.summary: Accurate, well-scoped Lane A script. All the key numbers check out against SURMOUNT-1 (NEJM 2022), SURPASS-1 (Lancet 2021), SURMOUNT-4 (JAMA 2024) and the label/guideline sources: arm sizes, weight loss by both estimands, the share reaching ≥5%, blood pressure, stopping because of side effects, A1C change and the share reaching A1C <7%, the 335/335 split and the +14.0% vs −5.5% result. Populations are stated correctly, side effects and safety caveats are present (fluids, protein/kidney, start gently, prescriber line, no switching or stopping), Dana is clearly labelled as made up, and the hook is paid off. Four minor wording fixes are listed below: framing of non-responders, two missing estimand labels, and the Zepbound indication.

issues.claim: Depending on dose, roughly nine to fifteen people in every hundred on tirzepatide did not reach five percent, even after seventy-two weeks.
issues.problem: The 85/89/91% figures use the treatment-regimen estimand, so the 9–15 not reaching 5% include people who stopped the medicine or had missing data. As written, it sounds as if they all took tirzepatide for the full 72 weeks.
issues.fix: Narration: "Now flip it around. Counting everyone randomized, including people who stopped the medicine, roughly nine to fifteen people in every hundred in the tirzepatide groups had not reached five percent at week seventy-two." On-screen: "9–15 in 100 under 5% at week 72 (all randomized)"

issues.claim: If you're a slower responder, you're not failing, and it's not a character flaw.
issues.problem: The people below 5% at week 72 are 'smaller responders', not 'slower' ones. 'Slower' implies they would catch up later, which the trial didn't show.
issues.fix: Narration: "That's what 'averages, not predictions' means. If your response is slower or smaller than average, you're not failing, and it's not a character flaw." On-screen: "Slower or smaller isn't failing"

issues.claim: 87, 92 and 88 percent reached A1C below 7% vs 19% on placebo
issues.problem: These are efficacy-estimand figures (on assigned treatment). s28 labels its estimand but s29 doesn't, and the muted-viewer card has no qualifier.
issues.fix: Narration: "Counting people while they stayed on treatment, eighty-seven, ninety-two and eighty-eight percent in the tirzepatide groups reached an A-one-C below seven percent by week forty, a common goal. On placebo, nineteen percent did." On-screen: "On treatment, A1C below 7%: 87% / 92% / 88% vs 19%"

issues.claim: Placebo group went back up by an average of fourteen percent, while the group that continued lost a further five point five percent.
issues.problem: −5.5% vs +14.0% is the treatment-regimen estimand (the efficacy estimand is −6.7%). Label it, as the SURMOUNT-1 scenes do.
issues.fix: Narration: "Over the next fifty-two weeks, counting everyone randomized, weight in the placebo group went back up by an average of fourteen percent, while the group that continued lost a further five point five percent."

issues.problem: Incomplete: in the US, Zepbound is also approved for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Not wrong, just incomplete.
issues.fix: Narration: "…sold as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for weight management and, in adults with obesity, moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea." (Optional.)

issues: Headline is intriguing but fairly generic/abstract; doesn't tie as directly to the title's 'how long' timing promise as the other two
Pen mascot with question mark communicates 'mystery' but not specifically about timing/duration

Subtitle 'THE TRIAL TIMELINE' is small and likely unreadable at phone/small size, reducing it to just '72 WEEKS' which could be misread as 'it takes 72 weeks to start working' — a different claim than the title promises (time-to-work vs trial length), risking a misleading impression
Giving away a specific number upfront narrows the curiosity gap compared to the other two candidates, likely lowering click motivation since viewers feel they already have 'the answer'
Clock/scale icon swap between row and small crops is consistent, but the mini '72 WEEKS' vs this one's simpler two-word headline reads faster — no major issues
Before/after device is a very common YouTube trope, slightly reducing novelty, but it's honest and directly answers the emotional tension in the title

thumbnail.reasoning: All three are clean, on-brand, legible at phone size with a single bold focal point and 2-4 words. #1 ('72 WEEKS') risks a subtle mismatch: it could be read as 'it takes 72 weeks to work,' which isn't what the video is actually about (time-to-first-effects vs. trial duration), and it also partially closes the curiosity gap the title opens, likely dulling click motivation. #0 ('WHAT CHANGES FIRST?') is a strong, honest curiosity hook but is a bit abstract and doesn't carry emotional stakes. #2 ('SLOW START?') pairs a tight curiosity question with a clear emotional before/after (worried face → relieved face) that mirrors the real viewer anxiety behind the title ('is this working yet?'), without overpromising — the scale imagery stays honest ('averages, not promises') and reads instantly at thumbnail size. That combination of emotional pull + honest curiosity + top-tier legibility makes it the best click driver while staying fully compliant with the title's promise.

issues.claim: Side effects were mostly mild-to-moderate GI issues, most common while the dose was raised.
issues.problem: The script says "gastrointestinal", not the abbreviation "GI". Packaging should use the script's wording, keep the abbreviation count low, and name a concrete common side effect so the line actually helps viewers.
issues.fix: Side effects were mostly mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal ones, like nausea and diarrhea, mainly while the dose was being raised.
